units.en: Defaults to always being true, making it disappear instantly
⟦0⟧, if set, turns the mission into one that where the player must select the button. If unset or set to false, then the complete effect will fire as soon as ⟦1⟧ is true.

⟦0⟧ decides on triggers that must be met for the decision to appear, assuming ⟦1⟧ was true on the game's start. This is checked daily. ⟦2⟧ The activate_mission = mission_name effect can bypass both allowed and activation, and it's usually better-optimised to use it to make the decision appear instead of relying on it being done automatically.
⟦0⟧ does nothing and shouldn't be used in missions.
The ⟦0⟧ ⟦1⟧ can bypass both ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧, and it's usually better-optimised to use it to make the decision appear instead of relying on it being done automatically.

⟦0⟧ changes the tooltips shown to the player on a non-selectable mission. By default or if set to false, the tooltip states that the ⟦1⟧ will complete the mission, calling ⟦2⟧ the effects if it's not completed. If set to true, ⟦3⟧ will instead change to "Effects when failed". This is purely graphical and may be used to better communicate to the player whether they should seek to complete the prerequisites or to avoid them being true.

⟦0⟧ will make the game assume that the mission, within its ⟦1⟧ will declare war on the specified country. This is used to make the AI prepare for a declaration of war and amass its troops on the border. This will also grant a notification to the target and all of its allies that a wargoal is being justified.
Other attributes, such as ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧ generally may be used inside of missions and should work how they do outside of them.

In addition to regular decisions that are taken by the country towards that same country, it is possible to make a decision be targeted towards a different country or group of countries. In that case, the decision will clone itself for each country that it gets targeted towards, putting the flag of the country in the bottom right of the decision's icon. The targeted country will be possible to reference in code using ⟦0⟧, while ROOT is still the country that gets the decision. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧, in this case, will make the decision fire only once per each target country: a decision targeted towards BLR will not disappear if a decision of the same ID targered towards LIT gets completed. Missions, as well as regular decisions, can be made targeted.
Despite what the names imply, FROM is the target of the decision rather than the country doing it.
A decision becomes targeted if any way to check for a target is added within the decision:
There are several ways to limit the selection of targets. If any of these three is present in the decision, it will be marked as targeted.

The primary way to limit the selection to a select few countries is ⟦0⟧. In that case, if you want the game to check every country with that original tag (including civil war rebellions and other types of dynamic countries), then ⟦1⟧ line of code will ensure that the game will check more than the country that the country tag truly belongs to. Additionally, by default, it's impossible to target a non-existing country. The ⟦2⟧ argument can be used to remove that restriction.
Additionally, it is possible to use ⟦0⟧ to limit a selection with ⟦1⟧, where the array must be assigned to the country. ⟦2⟧
You can see a list of arrays automatically generated by the game here.
Together with any of the previous two ways or without them, ⟦0⟧ is a trigger block evaluated daily for both FROM and ROOT, if ⟦1⟧ is evaluated as true.

For targeted decisions, ⟦0⟧ is also possible to use, as a trigger block that continuously checks every day if allowed was met, required to make the decision or the entire category be visible in the decision selection screen. ⟦1⟧, being executed before ⟦2⟧ is. This exists for optimisation purposes, as it takes much less time to check the condition for one country daily than for every combination of countries.
⟦0⟧ checks the country that should get this decision and only checks upon the game's start or when reloading decisions such as by loading a savegame. If false, the decision is permamently disabled.
⟦0⟧ checks the country the country that should get this decision, every day. If false, the decision will not appear until the next daily check. ⟦1⟧
Despite only checking one country, this still makes the decision targeted.

⟦0⟧ checks any countries (or states) that meet ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧, if they're present. In here, ROOT (default scope) is the country that gets the decision and FROM is the potential target of the decision. This is checked daily, making the decision not appear until the next day's check if false. Putting this automatically makes the decision targeted.
⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ are checked every tick. If the decision is targeted, then FROM is checked alongside ROOT, otherwise only ROOT is checked.
The regular arguments of ⟦0⟧ do not work if using FROM as a target. Instead, there are alternatives for targeted decisions specifically:
⟦0⟧ - Equivalent to ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ - Equivalent to ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ - Equivalent to ⟦5⟧

Similarly to missions, the ⟦0⟧ effect exists. If possible, it is recommended to use this effect instead of letting it automatically activate, making it never allowed. For instance, if the targeted decision activates by being at war with a country, ⟦1⟧ can be used to activate it instead of using ⟦2⟧.

If the decision has ⟦0⟧ then, instead, it'll be targeted towards a state. Possible values are: yes, no, any, any_owned_state, any_controlled_state, continent_key (europe, africa, north_america...). This will only have an effect if no 'targets' are specified, else this should be set to 'any' (or 'yes') if targets are used. Unless omitted or set to "no", makes the decision a state targeted decision. Which states will be checked depends on value: - any (or yes): will check every state in the game against the 'target_trigger'. - any_owned_state: will check every state owned by the country. This is equivalent to adding 'is_owned_by = ROOT' in the target_trigger. - any_controlled_state: will check every state controlled by the country. This is equivalent to adding 'is_controlled_by = ROOT' in the target_trigger. - continent_key (europe, africa, north_america...): will check every state in the continent. This is equivalent to adding 'is_on_continent = xxx' in the target_trigger.
When using explicit targets such as via ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧ only ⟦2⟧ will work the others will produce an error
Targeting still works the same way, with it having FROM as a state scope instead. ⟦0⟧ becomes ⟦1⟧ or, in case of one state total, ⟦2⟧ can be used as well.
Decisions targeted towards states will have the icon appear over the states while the decision menu is open. To prevent confusion, a ⟦0⟧ can be added to the decision category.
Additionally, The argument ⟦0⟧ will determine where the targeted decisions appear in.

⟦0⟧ will make the targeted decisions only appear on the map. ⟦1⟧ will make the targeted decisions only appear in the decisions menu. ⟦2⟧ will make the targeted decisions appear on both the map and the decisions menu.
